subject: Order Form discussion: SLA trade-offs, credits, and evidence request
messages:
From: Liam Chan <liam.chan@brightlane.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightLane Legal <legal@brightlane.com>; procurement@brightlane.com
Date: Thu, 22 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form: SLA trade-offs and evidence request

Hi Sofia / Marissa,

Thanks for the demo last week — BrightLane's infra team is aligned on the integration plan. Procurement and Legal asked me to escalate a couple of SLA items before we sign the Order Form so we can loop in our CISO for acceptance. High level asks: 

- Uptime target: your standard Order Form shows 99.95% for our region. We need justification for that vs 99.9% and the corresponding credit matrix. We may ask for a narrower window.
- Service credits: please propose the credit cadence for incremental buckets (e.g., <=99.5, 99.0).
- Response times: we need P1/P2 response commitments and an on-call escalation path (names/emails fine).
- Maintenance: proposed rolling window + max blackout per month. We need a clear maintenance exclusion definition.

Also: to get this through our security review we need a short SOC2 summary and a sample audit log schema (not full logs). If you can attach a 1-page SOC2 summary and the maintenance runbook excerpt, that would speed things up.

Attached is our initial redline doc (BrightLane-SLA-Proposed-Redlines.docx). Can you confirm if Redwood can accept the proposed credit caps or suggest trade-offs?

Thanks,
Liam
Liam Chan
Procurement Manager | BrightLane
liam.chan@brightlane.com

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chan <liam.chan@brightlane.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: SLA trade-offs and evidence request

Thanks, Liam — looping in Marissa (sales) and Kimberly (legal) to coordinate the redlines. Quick notes/clarifying Qs before we mark up your doc: 

1) Uptime/service credits: Redwood's standard for hosted customers in the US tier is 99.95% monthly uptime with the following credit bands: 99.9-99.95 -> 10% credit, 99.0-99.9 -> 30%, <99.0 -> 50% (applied to monthly invoice). We can discuss moving to 99.9 for enterprise accounts with a higher commit on dedicated capacity.

2) Response times: We commit to a 1-hour initial response for P1, 4 hours for P2, and 8 business hours for P3 (on-call 24/7 for P1s). We can enumerate the on-call escalation steps in the Order Form appendix.

3) Maintenance: We offer a rolling maintenance cadence with a default 4-hour single-event maintenance window and up to 10 hours/month total planned maintenance for hosted tenants. For Dedicated/Private customers we can expand or limit windows per contract. Please confirm whether BrightLane needs a stricter monthly cap.

Attached: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf (redacted), ops-maintenance-runbook-v1.md (excerpt). I uploaded a short Ops runbook snippet that explains our fallback to cross-region replicas during upgrades.

Kimberly — can Legal propose precise wording for “planned maintenance” exclusion (we currently exclude maintenance announced >=72 hours in advance and performed within agreed windows)?

Liam — if you prefer, Marissa can prepare a compromise counterproposal that balances credit exposure and our ability to guarantee throughput.

Best,
Sofia Ivanova
Head of Customer Success, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.com

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary.pdf; ops-maintenance-runbook-v1.md

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Liam Chan <liam.chan@brightlane.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.com>; Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>; Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 23 Apr 2027 11:08:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Order Form: SLA trade-offs and evidence request

Liam — thanks for sending the doc. I took a pass and sketched a practical middle ground that keeps risk shared and avoids open-ended credit exposure. Key proposal (summary):

- Uptime: agree to 99.95% as baseline. If BrightLane requires 99.9% baseline instead, we can support that by moving you to a "Reserved Dedicated" offering (higher commit + monthly fee).
- Credits: cap aggregate credits to 100% of one month's fees in any rolling 12-month period. Maintain the three-band credit % I listed earlier but scale them down by half if the customer is on Dedicated and we provide guaranteed capacity.
- Response SLAs: keep the P1/P2/P3 times Sofia proposed. Add an SLA credit only for P1s that meet a severity threshold (incident causing >25% request failure across customer tokens for >30 minutes).
- Maintenance: move to a max 8 hours/month planned maintenance window for BrightLane (instead of our default 10 hours) with an agreed blackout calendar for Q4. For emergency maintenance we provide advance notice as soon as feasible.

Legal/Commercial asks for Redwood: Kimberly, can you prepare redline language that implements the 12-month credit cap and the P1 severity threshold? Also, Connor, can Ops confirm that we can support a max 8-hour/month planned window without risk to change freeze cadence?

If that sounds acceptable we can incorporate the changes into the Order Form and send a DocuSign envelope with the MSA/Order Form bundle. I included a HubSpot link to the deal for reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/DL-4921

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director of Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

Attachment referenced: BrightLane-SLA-Proposed-Redlines.docx (we'll produce an internal markup to share next)

Forwarding a brief ops note for context:

--- Forwarded message ---
From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 24 Apr 2027 08:01:00 -0700
To: sofia_ivanova@redwood.com
Subject: technical note — maintenance mitigation and regional failover logic

Sofia — quick technical details to support the legal wording: 

- For hosted customers we run multi-AZ replicas and can failover read-only traffic within ~90s; full stateful failovers (write traffic with KV cache) can take up to 6 minutes depending on request rates.
- During planned maintenance we pre-warm secondary nodes and stage KV caches to reduce impact; this is why a 4-hour single-event window is usually sufficient. Increasing the monthly allowance to 8 hours is operationally okay but raises the probability of customer-visible latencies during large-scale rolling upgrades.
- Audit logs: we can provide an example schema (timestamp, request_id, route, model_id, tokens_consumed, latency_ms, outcome_code) but will not provide PII.

If you want, I can add a one-paragraph technical exhibit to the Order Form that describes the failover expectations and the audit-log sample schema.

Connor O'Brien
Head of Site Reliability | Redwood Inference
connor_obrien@redwood.com

Attachments: ops-maintenance-runbook-v1.md

- 8 hours/month planned maintenance max is acceptable with a Q4 blackout on major changes.
- P1 credit tied to the severity threshold you suggested is ok, but our Security team still wants the SOC2 summary and the audit-log schema before Legal will sign off.

Liam
